comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED — Gerrit change 1294, commit 8cc3e9abe0 (rebased onto the current gerrit tip
before pushing, so CI runs the target branch workflow against a current base).

THE FIX, and why the REVIEWERS OWN SUGGESTED FIX WAS REJECTED. The plan review that surfaced this bug
proposed "treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block`". I checked the spec before implementing it
and did NOT take that route, because it would introduce a second defect:
  code-review-verify.eval.yaml header: "Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of
    verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK verdict ... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set."
  dataset comment: "the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both."
BOTH cases — V-real-defect (gold block) and V-clean-rename (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a
non-empty list. Mapping presence to `block` would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the CLEAN
case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm carries no polarity, so no adapter can derive one.
Exclusion — the reviewers stated alternative — is the correct remedy.

SHAPE: `POLARITY_FREE_SOLVERS = frozenset({"code-review-verify"})` (provider_parity.py:101), excluded in
`solver_arm` (:172) alongside but SEPARATE FROM `AGENTIC_SOLVERS`. Kept separate deliberately: that set
excludes ops `gate_config` cannot reach, this one excludes a scorer with no decision to compare.
Collapsing them would lose a reason, and a future reader deleting the "redundant" set would silently
re-admit mis-scored cases. A test pins the disjointness for exactly that reason.

RED PROVEN BEHAVIOURALLY, not by an import error. I kept the constant defined and removed only the
exclusion from `solver_arm`, so the failures are real assertions rather than AttributeError:
  test_a_polarity_free_spec_is_excluded_from_the_corpus      FAILED  assert {code-review-verify} == set()
  test_the_polarity_free_exclusion_is_not_folded_into_the_agentic_one  FAILED  assert code-review is None
That is the defect stated as behaviour: the spec genuinely WAS eligible and DID resolve to an arm.

RE-SCORE, OFFLINE, ZERO MODEL CALLS (AC4). Rows from the excluded spec are RETAINED in the artifact for
provenance — the calls were really made — and dropped only from SCORING; deleting them would discard live
evidence. A `scoring_note` in each slot records why.
                        n_gold      recall v1 -> v2            gating verdict
  standard    28 -> 26   0.857 -> 0.923  /  0.929 -> 1.000     UNCHANGED (still 1 decision flip)
  frontier    28 -> 26   0.929 -> 1.000  /  0.929 -> 1.000     UNCHANGED (agreement 0.929 -> 0.923,
                                                                still below 0.95; still 2 flips)
NO GATING VERDICT CHANGED, as predicted — the miss was SYMMETRIC across both arms, so the v2-vs-v1
noninferiority comparison was never biased, and false-accept was untouched because the affected case is a
gold-BLOCK case, not a safe one. false_accept moves 0.214 -> 0.231 purely because the safe-item
denominator shrank 14 -> 13; the numerator is unchanged.
THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR THE EPIC: the mis-scored case was the ONLY recall miss on the BEDROCK arm.
Bedrocks true recall is 1.000, not the 0.929 previously recorded — the bug was understating the very
thing S6 exists to measure.
Slot-level `latency_s` is preserved (frontier 2103.3/2105.3, standard 2756.6/2484.8); only the nested
recomputed metrics block carries 0.0, which is inherent to an offline re-score that makes no calls.

GOLD FLOOR HOLDS: 26 >= MIN_GOLD_ITEMS (20), pinned by a test so a future exclusion cannot silently drop
the corpus below the floor.

GATES — all by exit code, clean tree, asserted EMPTY before the suite run so the result is evidence about
this commit:
  HEAD 8cc3e9abe0 · git status --porcelain: empty
  make lint = 0 · make typecheck = 0 · check_config_reads.py = 0 · gen_env_registry.py --check = 0
  pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal = EXIT 0
    9436 passed, 41 skipped, 1 xfailed in 474.84s
Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Will not close before Verified +1.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The provider-parity corpus includes the `code-review-verify` spec, whose output carries NO decision
polarity, so the two-bucket parity mapping cannot score it. Every verify case is therefore scored
`advisory` regardless of its gold label, which makes the gold-block case `V-real-defect` a GUARANTEED
recall miss on BOTH arms.

Confirmed empirically in the committed artifact
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`: `V-real-defect` has `label: "block"` with
`v1.decision == v2.decision == "advisory"`, `valid: true`, `errored: false`, on BOTH the standard and
frontier slots. Both verify cases sit inside the scored gold set (30 records, `n_gold` 28; the two
excluded are the `G3-*` container fixtures).

Mechanism: `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` (imported by `provider_parity.py:52` so the two
cannot drift) keys only on `verdict == "FAIL"` or a non-empty `findings`. The verifier emits neither —
its output vocabulary is `{verifications: [...]}` — so it falls through to `advisory`.

## Why the obvious fix is WRONG

"Treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block`" looks right and is not. `code-review-verify.eval.yaml`
states the contract twice:
  - header: "Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK
    verdict ... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set."
  - dataset: "the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both."
BOTH cases — `V-real-defect` (gold block) and `V-clean-rename` (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a
non-empty list. Mapping presence to `block` would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the clean
case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm has no polarity to read; no adapter can invent one.

## Approach

EXCLUDE `code-review-verify` from the parity corpus, for a reason DISTINCT from the existing
`AGENTIC_SOLVERS` exclusion (that one excludes agentic ops; this one excludes a polarity-free scorer).
Keep the two reasons separately named so a future reader does not collapse them.

## Impact on the recorded run

Excluding both verify cases takes `n_gold` 28 -> 26, still above `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20`. It removes one
guaranteed miss from each arm, so recall rises on both. The miss was SYMMETRIC, so no gating verdict
flips — the v2-vs-v1 noninferiority comparison is unaffected and false-accept is untouched (the affected
case is a gold-block case, not a safe one). This corrects measurement ACCURACY, not a pass/fail outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `code-review-verify` is excluded from the parity corpus by a named, separate mechanism from
      `AGENTIC_SOLVERS`, with the reason (no decision polarity) stated at the definition.
- [ ] A test asserts NO case from a polarity-free spec is eligible, and that the exclusion reason is
      distinct from the agentic exclusion — i.e. removing the agentic set does not silently cover this.
- [ ] A test pins the SPECIFIC failure this fixes: a `{verifications: [...]}` output does NOT map to
      `block`, AND a gold-block verify case is no longer scored as a live miss because it is excluded
      rather than mis-scored. It must fail before the fix.
- [ ] The recorded artifact is RE-SCORED OFFLINE with zero model calls; the new `n_gold` and recall are
      recorded, and it is stated explicitly whether any GATING verdict changed (expected: none).
- [ ] The gold floor still holds after exclusion (`n_gold >= MIN_GOLD_ITEMS`), asserted by a test so a
      future corpus shrink cannot silently drop below it.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, the default selection is green, and the
      config-read and env-drift gates pass.
compiled_state.title: Parity corpus scores the polarity-free code-review-verify arm, guaranteeing a recall miss
